---
title: "Materials, stack and Z mapping"
description: "Produce the requested physical or thin-film model without losing layer or material meaning."
sidebar: simulation
---

The model must identify which metal/dielectric representation produced the
result. OrPen supplies physical process facts; the simulation case chooses
the approximation.

## Input supplied by OrPen

- Material identity/properties and explicit native-library or ideal-conductor intent.
- Physical layer identities, aliases, layer/datatype selectors and body membership.
- Z intervals, thicknesses, host die and lower/upper contact orientation.
- Stack-bearing film, local deck/film and retained post/bump declarations.

Interface-loss film thickness is separate from metal thickness. Source
superconducting identity does not authorize an invented kinetic-inductance model.

## Backend requirements

::: {.panel-tabset}

### Palace

| Model choice | Required delivery |
| --- | --- |
| Finite metal | Represent the requested Route B metal boundary/exclusion and remaining dielectric/air solution domain. |
| Sheet approximation | State the selected Route A sheet location and treatment of the metal interval and surrounding domain. |
| Physical-level collapse | Keep physical/effective dimensions and interface locations attributable; no unexplained shift of upper geometry. |
| Multilevel structures | Preserve post/bump endpoints and conductor interfaces under the declared route. |
| Materials | Assign explicit properties to material regions and boundaries. |

### AEDT

| Model choice | Required delivery |
| --- | --- |
| Finite metal | Build solid conductors at the declared physical intervals. |
| Sheet approximation | State the selected thin-film map and effective sheet contact plane. |
| Physical-level collapse | Collapse a stack-bearing interval once per physical level; local deck thickness must not compress surrounding stack. |
| Multilevel structures | Retain posts/bumps as solids under the same Z map, without inferred extension. |
| Materials | Assign native material/PEC treatment with original physical material identity retained. |

:::

Route A/B and solid/thin-film are different backend model choices, not names
for interchangeable geometry. Q2D uses explicitly authored section materials
and thickness, not an automatic 3D stack collapse.

## Final product to inspect

A physical-to-effective Z table plus native material and cross-section views.
Include conductor, substrate, Region, supports/ports and upper structures.
Historical outputs retain the stack that was actually used.

Candidates: SimplePad for the base film, airbridge for local deck/posts and
flip-chip for opposing faces/bumps.
[Process and source views](../../public-pdk-examples/test-components.md).

::: {.callout-note title="Inspect physical and effective heights together"}

[Multilevel contacts](../../notebooks/ComponentSimulation/GeometrySemantics/geometry_multilevel_contacts.ipynb)
provides the physical source view for bumps, posts and decks.
[SimplePad Q3D](../../notebooks/ComponentSimulation/SimplePad/aedt_q3d.ipynb)
and [SimplePad HFSS EPR](../../notebooks/ComponentSimulation/SimplePad/aedt_hfss_eigenmode.ipynb)
provide the corresponding Solid/Thin Film case choices. Inspect the prepared
Z map, then native body/sheet extents and material assignments; a source stack
table alone does not demonstrate those native observations.

:::

For Thin Film, distinguish the base stack-bearing film from the local bridge
deck: remove the former interval once per physical identity, not once per
bump or polygon. Map each retained post/bump endpoint with the same stack map.
The deck becomes a sheet at its declared contact side without shortening the
surrounding stack by its own thickness.

Serves [capacitance](../requirements/electrostatic-capacitance.qmd),
[eigenmode](../requirements/eigenmode.qmd), [EPR](../requirements/epr-loss.qmd),
[driven terminal](../requirements/driven-terminal.qmd) and [Q3D](../requirements/q3d-acrl.qmd).
